key_insight: ProtoDiffusion represents a layered graphic design using one shared spatial prototype and one compact vector per layer, rather than a separate spatial grid for every layer. This makes the representation less dependent on the combined spatial extent of the layers.
problem_solved: Existing models represent each RGBA layer with a full-canvas or region-sized latent grid, causing representation size to grow with the cumulative area of the layers. The challenge is to model layered designs more compactly while retaining their editable structure.
method: Use ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder, to encode a design into a shared spatial prototype.
Represent each layer with a candidate vector instead of its own spatial latent grid.
Build a latent-diffusion generative framework on this representation.
impact: This approach offers a potentially more compact foundation for generating layered graphics that support selection, movement, and reuse. The supplied abstract is truncated, so quantitative efficiency gains and generation-quality results cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: An exploded stack of RGBA layers illustrating an editable graphic design.

paper_title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
paper_authors: Adrià Ciurana Lanau, Harleen Hanspal, Lusine Abrahamyan, Emilio Tylson Baixauli, Yu Cao
